correctness.rationale: The odd-degree Kummer presentation w=xty has degree 3M (the commuting cyclic actions act faithfully on w), with ramification gcds 1,M,1. The gcds at zero and infinity use gcd(M,3)=1 and M=2 mod 3, and tame Riemann–Hurwitz gives M. Local valuations make a differential holomorphic exactly when the two fractional parts sum to more than one. Counting by the CRT for (i mod 3,i mod M) gives M pairwise distinct characters. For 2j=i mod 3M the remaining factors after extracting a square are t and t+1 to exponents 0 or 1. When i is in the basis, if j is not in it, a nonzero such digit would force the doubled fractional-parts sum to be at most one. The Cartier rules thus give precisely the asserted partial inverse-doubling permutation; its stable image is the span of complete surviving cycles, which gives the two-rank, not merely the rank of one Cartier application. The residue-one two-step condition is u in (1/6,1/3) or (2/3,5/6). For branch choices a,b, the inverse map from J_b to J_a is x -> (x+2a+1-b)/4. Composing along a word and adjoining the reflected terminal symbol gives one fixed point of the reflected contraction; its denominator divides 4^h+1, so it cannot hit a boundary with denominator three or six. This proves existence and uniqueness of each itinerary, and 4^h=-1 mod M makes those tests sufficient for the entire orbit. Doubling exchanges the two nonzero residue classes, giving 2^(h+1). Bounded independent replay: python3 /workspace/reproductions/frozen_checks.py rank constructs and checks the base-four digit witnesses for h=1..10. It is not a proof of the rank theorem or a reproduction of the frozen finite-field zeta computation. Frozen verification code and notes were inspected, not executed.
